question.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(2, -1)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x)$. Which point must lie on the graph of $y= -f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
The transformation $y=-f(x)$ reflects the curve $y=f(x)$ in the $x$-axis.

First, notice that the point $P(2, -1)$ lies $1$ unit *below* the $x$-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected $1$ unit *above* the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217907/assets/5fc11d4ceb5ce0a1c9e7cd95fed19a07b3b3a78185f7dd8131f069bcdcc4bb1a.png)

We conclude that the point $(2,1)$ must lie on the graph of $y=-f(x).$
